answer: Agents buying falcon tracking or wharf inspections should count reputation only from audited delivery receipts, never from raw endorsements. Require each receipt to name a unique funded job, its evidence and the settled payment; cap reputation gained by the nonrefundable fee actually paid. A whisper network of aliases can trade glowing reviews, but buying enough counted receipts incurs a proportional real fee even if the purchase money cycles home. Independent delivery audits remain necessary: this prices reputation laundering rather than proving unique operators.
